findings.title: View-only permission authorizes top-level group creation and moves
findings.body: canManage() accepts either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on requireManage(), which calls this method, so an administrator granted only VIEW can create top-level groups or move existing groups to the top level. This check must require MANAGE rather than treating read access as write access.

findings.title: Group search restriction uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() searches resources by the Groups type and passes/adds groupResource.getId(). However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates individual authorization resources with the group ID as their name, gives them a separate generated resource ID, and does not set their type. Consequently individual group resources are not found by this scan; the typed all-groups resource can instead contribute its authorization ID, which is not a group ID. UsersResource uses this set to restrict user searches and counts by group membership, causing permitted members to disappear or counts to be incorrect. Enumerate the actual group resources/groups and evaluate and return model group IDs, not authorization resource IDs.

findings.title: Group membership restriction excludes users authorized individually
findings.body: When an administrator lacks global user-view permission but has both an individual user-view permission and view-members permission on a group, searchForUser sets UserModel.GROUPS to only the permitted groups. The user provider then restricts the search to those memberships before canView is evaluated. An individually authorized user outside those groups is therefore omitted even though GET by user ID succeeds. The search must include the union of individually authorized users and users authorized through groups rather than applying the group restriction to all results. The same issue affects the corresponding brute-force user search.
